- When sentiment turns negative (especially after a spike), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67+ changes), model often overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.  
- After a sharp price drop, model frequently underreacts — add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often misses downward trend — adjust downward by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — use 3-day moving average of recent 10-day history to smooth forecast.  
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model often underestimates true decline — add 1–3% to forecast to account for lagged sentiment effect.
